The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

To understand inflation theory in cosmology, imagine a tiny, wrinkled raisin dough ball. Inflation is like the moment that dough is placed in a hot oven and expands incredibly fast. In just a fraction of a second, the dough grows so large that any wrinkles or small details on its surface become stretched out and appear flat and uniform, even though the dough itself is now massive. Similarly, the early universe expanded so rapidly that it smoothed out irregularities, creating the large-scale structure we see today. This expansion happened faster than the speed of light, not because matter moved through space faster than light, but because space itself was stretching.
